title: Definitive Sanctification
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Definitive sanctification means that believers have been decisively set apart for God in Christ and are no longer slaves of sin. It describes a real break with sin’s ruling dominion, not the completion of all growth.
summary: Definitive sanctification means that believers have been decisively set apart for God in Christ and are no longer slaves of sin. It describes a real break with sin’s ruling dominion, not the completion of all growth.
christFocus: Jesus Christ sets His people apart through His death and resurrection. Those united to Him have died to sin’s old mastery and now belong to God as people made alive in Christ.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Sanctification has both a decisive and progressive aspect. Believers are being made holy over time, but they have also already been set apart in Christ.

Romans 6 teaches that believers united to Christ have died to sin and are alive to God. Sin remains a real battle, but it is no longer the believer’s rightful master.

Definitive sanctification does not mean believers are sinless. It means their identity and ownership have changed. They are washed, sanctified, justified, and transferred into Christ’s kingdom.

This doctrine gives a foundation for fighting sin. Believers do not fight as slaves trying to become free; they fight as those set free by Christ and called to live in that freedom.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Some believers think their struggle with sin means nothing has changed. Others use grace as an excuse to remain under sin’s rule. Definitive sanctification speaks to both errors.

This doctrine is especially helpful for those coming out of addiction or bondage. In Christ, the old master no longer has final claim. The fight may be real, but the believer is not what he once was.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Count yourself dead to sin and alive to God in Christ. Do not surrender to sin as though it still owns you. Bring your body, habits, desires, and choices under the lordship of Christ, trusting that He has truly set you apart for God.
